full_judgment: 27. In our view, allegations of corruption or criminal conduct cannot and should not be stopped, but a duty is cast upon the investigating agency and also on the court to judge whether the allegation merits consideration for prosecution. We further hold that the yardstick to be followed in such cases is not a mere reversal of a decision of lower ranking public servant by his higher authority, rather the yardstick is whether the decision show a clear and manifest abuse of the official position. However there is no set rule that may be followed by the investigating agency or by the judge for detecting an action or omission as a clear and manifest abuse of power. Each and every case has to be meticulously examined for arriving at a just and proper decision.
